<!-- Generated by tools/cli-reference.py from `backdown daemon --help`. Edit the help in crates/backdown-cli (or the notes in the script) and run it again. -->


```text
backdown daemon [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

`--port <PORT>`
: Port for the web UI (0: any free one). Default: `8787`. Also read from `$BACKDOWN_PORT`.

`--host <HOST>` {preview}
: Also listen on this address (e.g. this computer's Tailscale IP) so other devices can look; from there BackDown only shows, and changes need this computer. 127.0.0.1 always listens. Default: `127.0.0.1`.

`--rescan-every <RESCAN_EVERY>`
: Rescan each drive this often (e.g. 12h, 1d; `never` to scan only on request or when a drive comes back). Default: as set in Settings (24h unless changed there).

`--system`
: Machine-wide service: index in /var/lib/backdown, socket in /run/backdown, shared with the `backdown` group (set by the system unit).

Also takes the [global options](/docs/cli/#global-options) `--db` and `--local`.

## Good to know

One job at a time (scan, hash, recognise, copy, mirror, wipe, tidy, mail merge), so the index has a single writer and each drive a single reader; rescues and syncs with other machines run beside them, and drive health is read every six hours. Every scan is followed by hashing, and recognition when something changed. Without `--rescan-every`, the interval is the one in Settings. `--host` works as for `serve`: the browser stays on 127.0.0.1 too, and from other devices it only shows and queues rescans (the link is `http://ADDRESS:PORT/?t=TOKEN`, with the token from `ui.json` in the data folder). On Linux and macOS the CLI talks to it through a socket in your runtime folder; on Windows, commands use the index directly.

## Examples

```sh
# usually started by `backdown service install`; by hand:
backdown daemon
backdown daemon --rescan-every 12h
# scan only when asked, or when a drive comes back
backdown daemon --rescan-every never
```
